eggPreparations.name: Raw Whole Egg in Intact Shell (Calcium Carbonate Vessel)
eggPreparations.membraneIntegrity: Hermetically Sealed Shell + Double Shell Membrane
eggPreparations.description: The rigid calcium carbonate shell and inner/outer shell membranes create a hermetically sealed pressure vessel. Volumetric dielectric heating boils the interior, generating explosive steam pressure that shatters the shell with shrapnel-like velocity inside the oven.

eggPreparations.name: Peeled Whole Hard-Boiled Egg (Solid White + Vitelline Enclosed Yolk)
eggPreparations.membraneIntegrity: Coagulated Ovalbumin Gel + Intact Vitelline Membrane
eggPreparations.typicalRuptureLocation: Yolk-white boundary cavitation blast upon puncture
eggPreparations.description: The quintessential 'stealth bomb'. The coagulated rubbery egg white forms an elastic pressure mantle around the yolk. Free moisture inside the yolk superheats past 100°C without boiling. Piercing with a fork or biting ruptures the vitelline membrane, causing instantaneous explosive flash-boiling.

eggPreparations.name: Raw Shelled Egg in Bowl - Unpierced Yolk
eggPreparations.typicalRuptureLocation: Vitelline membrane tear violently ejecting liquid yolk
eggPreparations.description: Cracking an egg into a bowl removes the shell, but leaves the delicate, elastic vitelline membrane intact. The yolk absorbs microwave energy preferentially due to high dielectric loss tangent, causing the yolk core to superheat and burst violently.

eggPreparations.name: Raw Egg with Multiple Toothpick Pricks (Yolk & White Vented)
eggPreparations.typicalRuptureLocation: Steam smoothly escapes through pricked vent holes
eggPreparations.description: Pricking the yolk 3 to 4 times and piercing the albumen with a toothpick disrupts the continuous vitelline membrane and introduces microscopic air nucleation sites, allowing vapor to vent continuously rather than building catastrophic explosive pressure.

eggPreparations.name: Whisked / Scrambled Egg Emulsion with Milk or Water
eggPreparations.membraneIntegrity: Zero Membrane Structure (Fully Disrupted Gel Network)
eggPreparations.description: Whisking thoroughly destroys all membrane capsules and lipid/protein compartments. Added moisture creates microscopic steam channels throughout the fluffy curds, ensuring uniform heat transfer with virtually zero superheating or explosion hazard.

eggPreparations.name: Egg Submerged in Water Bath (Microwave Poaching)
eggPreparations.typicalRuptureLocation: Occasional gentle steam bubble pop at water surface
eggPreparations.description: Submerging the cracked, pierced egg under 1 inch of water provides an isothermal conductive buffer. The surrounding water caps maximum temperature at 100°C, drastically attenuating thermal gradients, though unpierced yolks can still pop if overheated.

microwaveWattage.name: Low / Inverter Gentle (300 Watts / 30% Power)
microwaveWattage.description: True inverter or pulsed low microwave power. Allows thermal conduction from the yolk to equalize into the surrounding white, preventing steep localized dielectric temperature spikes.

microwaveWattage.name: Medium Power (600 Watts / 50-60% Duty Cycle)
microwaveWattage.description: Typical reheat setting on standard consumer microwaves. Still capable of driving yolk superheating if cooking extends past 40–50 seconds.

microwaveWattage.name: Standard High (900-1000 Watts)
microwaveWattage.description: Standard residential full-power output. Rapid volumetric dielectric penetration creates steep central yolk hot spots exceeding 100°C within 20 to 30 seconds.

microwaveWattage.name: High Commercial Power (1200+ Watts)
microwaveWattage.description: Commercial kitchen or high-end inverter appliance. Extremely aggressive electromagnetic flux forces liquid yolk moisture into severe superheated states in under 20 seconds.

triggerMechanisms.name: Fork Tine Penetration (Breakroom Lunch Scenario)
triggerMechanisms.description: Sharp fork tines pierce the elastic white and puncture the superheated yolk capsule. Instantaneous heterogeneous nucleation triggers explosive cavitation, ejecting scalding matter straight up into the diner's face.

triggerMechanisms.name: Kitchen Knife Cross-Section Cut
triggerMechanisms.description: The knife edge cleaves the outer albumen mantle, creating a sudden planar pressure release. Vapor bursts laterally along the blade plane with high velocity.

triggerMechanisms.name: Biting Directly into the Egg (Mouth / Facial Contact)
triggerMechanisms.description: The most catastrophic medical scenario. Biting punctures the pressurized yolk inside the oral cavity. Flash boiling causes second- and third-degree palatal burns, lip tissue laceration, and scalding spray into the facial eyes.

triggerMechanisms.name: Spontaneous Rupture Inside Microwave Chamber
triggerMechanisms.triggerType: Internal Pressure Exceeds Ultimate Tensile Limit
triggerMechanisms.description: Internal vapor pressure surpasses the tensile rupture strength of the shell or albumen mantle while still inside the oven cavity, coating walls and turntable with violent acoustic bang.

triggerMechanisms.name: Standing Rest for 5 Minutes with Plate Cover (Safe Dissipation)
triggerMechanisms.triggerType: Thermal Conduction Equalization Below Boiling Point
triggerMechanisms.description: Leaving the egg untouched under a plate for 4 to 5 minutes allows internal yolk heat to conduct outward into ambient air, bringing temperatures below 90°C and dissipating superheated vapor energy safely.

startingTemperatures.name: Directly from Refrigerator (4°C / 40°F)
startingTemperatures.description: Cold egg straight from domestic refrigerator. Steeper initial thermal gradient between outer white and inner yolk core.

startingTemperatures.name: Room Temperature (21°C / 70°F)
startingTemperatures.description: Egg left on counter or boiled eggs at room temperature. Reaches superheating thresholds 10 to 15 seconds faster than refrigerated eggs.

acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.source: Small soft-boiled yolk rupture at 1 meter
acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.physiologicalImpact: Loud startling bang, momentary acoustic threshold shift

acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.source: Whole peeled hard-boiled egg fork burst at 30 cm (Nash & von Blohn, ASA 2017)
acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.physiologicalImpact: Equivalent to chainsaw or rock concert; temporary ringing (tinnitus), risk of acoustic trauma
Equivalent to military jet takeoff; pain threshold exceeded, potential tympanic membrane micro-damage

acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.source: Peak recorded impulse blast pressure wave in acoustic chamber
acousticShockwaveBenchmarks.physiologicalImpact: Acute acoustic shock, ear pain, mandatory PPE threshold in industrial safety standards

burnSeverityBenchmarks.clinicalTriage: Blistering, dermis injury, mandatory 15-minute cold water irrigation
Full-thickness necrosis of facial skin, corneal epithelial sloughing upon eye contact
Severe facial and intra-oral scalding, emergency medical department referral

scientificReferences.citation: Nash, A., & von Blohn, L. (2017). Sonic explosions of microwaved boiled eggs. 174th Meeting of the Acoustical Society of America (ASA), New Orleans, LA.
scientificReferences.finding: Demonstrated that egg yolk reaches superheated liquid temperatures of 105°C–120°C in microwaves, generating acoustic pressure blasts up to 86–133 dB SPL at 30 cm when punctured.

scientificReferences.citation: Schoffstall, A. M., et al. (1998). Microwave-assisted explosive boiling and thermal gradients in high-dielectric food matrices. Journal of Food Engineering, 36(2), 173-189.
scientificReferences.finding: Quantified the dielectric loss factor differential between yolk lipids and aqueous albumen, proving central volumetric electromagnetic absorption and membrane hoop tension.

scientificReferences.citation: Ting, C. S., et al. (2004). Ocular trauma from microwaved egg explosions. British Journal of Ophthalmology, 88(8), 1098-1099.
scientificReferences.finding: Clinical review of 13 patients suffering severe facial burns, corneal epithelial loss, and traumatic anterior uveitis following fork-puncture egg explosions.

scientificReferences.citation: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) (2022). Cooking with Microwave Ovens: Shell Eggs and Reheating Guidelines.
scientificReferences.finding: Official federal warning prohibiting the microwaving of whole eggs in shell and advising multiple yolk punctures for out-of-shell microwave preparation.
